newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Allianz in its home market.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Allianz in its home market.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN
Dr Reiner Hagemann, Allianz's head of German property and casualty business, yesterday gave an impressive presentation of the group's performance in its key market.

Allianz's German property/casualty operation managed to lift pre-tax profits by 471 million marks to 1.607 billion marks mainly from two sources: underwriting improved by 121 million marks to a profit of 944 million marks in a year with no major storm loss and an all-time low in German motor claims frequencies. In addition, Allianz realised gains of 420 million marks by selling mainly fixed-interest securities.
However, far more striking than the financial data were the details of Allianz's fight to regain market share and hold the initiative in the German market.

While bringing down its prices to undercut most other traditional insurers with a large force of tied agents, Allianz is also trying to improve service to overcome its price disadvantage compared with low-cost operators such as HUK-Coburg.

In a recent customer survey, Allianz found that 78 percent see speedy claims settlement as their main demand. As a result, Allianz insisted all claims reported to agents have to be faxed to the relevant back office within 48 hours. Customer use of the group's 24-hour claims hotline soared to 35,000 in 1996 compared with 6,000 the year before, and backoffice staff agreed to flexible working hours to cater to customers and agents.

In three cities Allianz has started field tests with dual motor pricing. As an alternative to installing a direct-selling company based on experience gathered from its Cornhill subsidiary in the UK, Allianz is giving its agents a second product which is 10 percent cheaper and slightly less attractive, so that the agent can remain competitive. All this is based on the largest database on German insurance, which makes risk selection for the market leader far easier than for anyone else.

All this is paying off - after years of losing business, Allianz managed a net gain of 40,000 motor risks last year, bringing it to eight million insured vehicles. In industrial business, too, it is seeking to regain the initiative by launching new product details that competitors will find hard to match.
In fact in many respects, Allianz is still calling the tune in the German market, and the rest will have to follow.
